verses.zh: 「以色列人哪，现在我所教训你们的律例典章，你们要听从遵行，好叫你们存活，得以进入耶和华―你们列祖之　神所赐给你们的地，承受为业。
verses.en: Now, Israel, pay attention to the statutes and ordinances[NOTE:1] I am about to teach you, so that you might live and go on to enter and take possession of the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors,[NOTE:2] is giving you.
notes: These technical Hebrew terms (חֻקִּים [khuqqim] and מִשְׁפָּטִים [mishpatim]) occur repeatedly throughout the Book of Deuteronomy to describe the covenant stipulations to which Israel had been called to subscribe (see, in this chapter alone, vv. 1, 5, 6, 8). The word חֻקִּים derives from the verb חֹק (khoq, “to inscribe; to carve”) and מִשְׁפָּטִים (mishpatim) from שָׁפַט (shafat, “to judge”). They are virtually synonymous and are used interchangeably in Deuteronomy.
Heb “fathers” (also in vv. 31, 37).

verses.zh: 所吩咐你们的话，你们不可加添，也不可删减，好叫你们遵守我所吩咐的，就是耶和华―你们　神的命令。
verses.en: Do not add a thing to what I command you nor subtract from it, so that you may keep the commandments of the Lord your God that I am delivering to[NOTE:1] you.
notes: Heb “commanding.”

verses.zh: 耶和华因巴力・毗珥的事所行的，你们亲眼看见了。凡随从巴力・毗珥的人，耶和华―你们的　神都从你们中间除灭了。
verses.en: You have witnessed what the Lord did at Baal Peor,[NOTE:1] how he[NOTE:2] eradicated from your midst everyone who followed Baal Peor.[NOTE:3]
notes: The LXX and Syriac read “to Baal Peor,” that is, the god worshiped at that place; see note on the name “Beth Peor” in Deut 3:29.
Heb “the Lord your God.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
Or “followed the Baal of Peor” (so NAB, NIV, NRSV), referring to the pagan god Baal.

verses.zh: 惟有你们专靠耶和华―你们　神的人，今日全都存活。
verses.en: But you who remained faithful to the Lord your God are still alive to this very day, every one of you.

verses.zh: 我照着耶和华―我　神所吩咐的将律例典章教训你们，使你们在所要进去得为业的地上遵行。
verses.en: Look! I have taught you statutes and ordinances just as the Lord my God told me to do, so that you might carry them out in[NOTE:1] the land you are about to enter and possess.
notes: Heb “in the midst of” (so ASV).

verses.zh: 所以你们要谨守遵行；这就是你们在万民眼前的智慧、聪明。他们听见这一切律例，必说：『这大国的人真是有智慧，有聪明！』
verses.en: So be sure to do them, because this will testify of your wise understanding[NOTE:1] to the people who will learn of all these statutes and say, “Indeed, this great nation is a very wise[NOTE:2] people.”
notes: Heb “it is wisdom and understanding.”
Heb “wise and understanding.”

verses.zh: 哪一大国的人有　神与他们相近，像耶和华―我们的　神、在我们求告他的时候与我们相近呢？
verses.en: In fact, what other great nation has a god so near to them like the Lord our God whenever we call on him?

verses.zh: 又哪一大国有这样公义的律例典章、像我今日在你们面前所陈明的这一切律法呢？
verses.en: And what other great nation has statutes and ordinances as just[NOTE:1] as this whole law[NOTE:2] that I am about to share with[NOTE:3] you today?
notes: Or “pure”; or “fair”; Heb “righteous.”

The Hebrew phrase הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת (hattorah hazzot), in this context, refers specifically to the Book of Deuteronomy. That is, it is the collection of all the חֻקִּים (khuqqim, “statutes,” 4:1) and מִשְׁפָּטִים (mishpatim, “ordinances,” 4:1) to be included in the covenant text. In a full canonical sense, of course, it pertains to the entire Pentateuch or Torah.
Heb “place before.”

verses.zh: 「你只要谨慎，殷勤保守你的心灵，免得忘记你亲眼所看见的事，又免得你一生、这事离开你的心；总要传给你的子子孙孙。
verses.en: Again, however, pay very careful attention,[NOTE:1] lest you forget the things you have seen and disregard them for the rest of your life; instead teach them to your children and grandchildren.
notes: Heb “watch yourself and watch your soul carefully.”

verses.zh: 你在何烈山站在耶和华―你　神面前的那日，耶和华对我说：『你为我招聚百姓，我要叫他们听见我的话，使他们存活在世的日子，可以学习敬畏我，又可以教训儿女这样行。』
verses.en: You[NOTE:1] stood before the Lord your God at Horeb and he[NOTE:2] said to me, “Assemble the people before me so that I can tell them my commands.[NOTE:3] Then they will learn to revere me all the days they live in the land, and they will instruct their children.”
notes: The text begins with “(the) day (in) which.” In the Hebrew text v. 10 is subordinate to v. 11, but for stylistic reasons the translation treats v. 10 as an independent clause, necessitating the omission of the subordinating temporal phrase at the beginning of the verse.
Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 4:3.
Heb “my words.” See v. 13; in Hebrew the “ten commandments” are the “ten words.”

verses.zh: 那时你们近前来，站在山下；山上有火焰冲天，并有昏黑、密云、幽暗。
verses.en: You approached and stood at the foot of the mountain, a mountain ablaze to the sky above it[NOTE:1] and yet dark with a thick cloud.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “a mountain burning with fire as far as the heart of the heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.
Heb “darkness, cloud, and heavy cloud.”

verses.zh: 耶和华从火焰中对你们说话，你们只听见声音，却没有看见形像。
verses.en: Then the Lord spoke to you from the middle of the fire; you heard speech but you could not see anything—only a voice was heard.[NOTE:1]
notes: The words “was heard” are supplied in the translation to avoid the impression that the voice was seen.

verses.zh: 他将所吩咐你们当守的约指示你们，就是十条诫，并将这诫写在两块石版上。
verses.en: And he revealed to you the covenant[NOTE:1] he has commanded you to keep, the Ten Commandments,[NOTE:2] writing them on two stone tablets.
notes: This is the first occurrence of the word בְּרִית (berit, “covenant”) in the Book of Deuteronomy but it appears commonly hereafter (4:23, 31; 5:2, 3; 7:9, 12; 8:18; 9:9, 10, 11, 15; 10:2, 4, 5, 8; 17:2; 29:1, 9, 12, 14, 15, 18, 21, 25; 31:9, 16, 20, 25, 26; 33:9). Etymologically, it derives from the notion of linking or yoking together. See M. Weinfeld, TDOT 2:255.
Heb “the ten words.”

verses.zh: 那时耶和华又吩咐我将律例典章教训你们，使你们在所要过去得为业的地上遵行。」
verses.en: Moreover, at that same time the Lord commanded me to teach you statutes and ordinances for you to keep in the land that you are about to enter and possess.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to which you are crossing over to possess it.”

verses.zh: 「所以，你们要分外谨慎；因为耶和华在何烈山、从火中对你们说话的那日，你们没有看见甚么形像。
verses.en: Be very careful,[NOTE:1] then, because you saw no form at the time the Lord spoke to you at Horeb from the middle of the fire.
notes: Heb “give great care to your souls.”

verses.zh: 惟恐你们败坏自己，雕刻偶像，彷佛甚么男像女像，
verses.en: I say this[NOTE:1] so you will not corrupt yourselves by making an image in the form of any kind of figure. This includes the likeness of a human male or female,
notes: The words “I say this” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. In the Hebrew text v. 16 is subordinated to “Be careful” in v. 15, but this makes for an unduly long sentence in English.

verses.zh: 或地上走兽的像，或空中飞鸟的像，
verses.en: any kind of land animal, any bird that flies in the sky,

verses.zh: 或地上爬物的像，或地底下水中鱼的像。
verses.en: anything that crawls[NOTE:1] on the ground, or any fish in the deep waters under the earth.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “creeping thing.”
Heb “under the earth.”

verses.zh: 又恐怕你向天举目观看，见耶和华―你的　神为天下万民所摆列的日月星，就是天上的万象，自己便被勾引敬拜事奉它。
verses.en: When you look up[NOTE:1] to the sky[NOTE:2] and see the sun, moon, and stars—the whole heavenly creation[NOTE:3]—you must not be seduced to worship and serve them,[NOTE:4] for the Lord your God has assigned[NOTE:5] them to all the people[NOTE:6] of the world.[NOTE:7]
notes: Heb “lest you lift up your eyes.” In the Hebrew text vv. 16-19 are subordinated to “Be careful” in v. 15, but this makes for an unduly long sentence in English.
Or “heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.
Heb “all the host of heaven.”

In the Hebrew text the verbal sequence in v. 19 is “lest you look up…and see…and be seduced…and worship them…and serve them.” However, the first two actions are not prohibited in and of themselves. The prohibition pertains to the final three actions. The first two verbs describe actions that are logically subordinate to the following actions and can be treated as temporal or circumstantial: “lest, looking up…and seeing…, you are seduced.” See Joüon 2:635 §168.h.
Or “allotted.”
Or “nations.”

Heb “under all the heaven.”sn The OT views the heavenly host as God’s council, which surrounds his royal throne ready to do his bidding (see 1 Kgs 22:19). God has given this group, sometimes called the “sons of God” (cf. Job 1:6; 38:7; Ps 89:6), jurisdiction over the nations. See Deut 32:8 (LXX). Some also see this assembly as the addressee in Ps 82. While God delegated his council to rule over the nations, he established a theocratic government over Israel and ruled directly over his chosen people via the Mosaic covenant. See v. 20, as well as Deut 32:9.

verses.zh: 耶和华将你们从埃及领出来，脱离铁炉，要特作自己产业的子民，像今日一样。
verses.en: You, however, the Lord has selected and brought from Egypt, that iron-smelting furnace,[NOTE:1] to be his special people[NOTE:2] as you are today.
notes: A כּוּר (kur) was not a source of heat but a crucible (“iron-smelting furnace”) in which precious metals were melted down and their impurities burned away (see I. Cornelius, NIDOTTE 2:618-19); cf. NAB “that iron foundry, Egypt.” The term is a metaphor for intense heat. Here it refers to the oppression and suffering Israel endured in Egypt. Since a crucible was used to burn away impurities, it is possible that the metaphor views Egypt as a place of refinement to bring Israel to a place of submission to divine sovereignty.
Heb “to be his people of inheritance.” The Lord compares his people to valued property inherited from one’s ancestors and passed on to one’s descendants.

verses.zh: 耶和华又因你们的缘故向我发怒，起誓必不容我过约旦河，也不容我进入耶和华―你　神所赐你为业的那美地。
verses.en: But the Lord became angry with me because of you and vowed that I would never cross the Jordan nor enter the good land that he[NOTE:1] is about to give you.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 4:3.
The Hebrew text includes “(as) an inheritance,” or “(as) a possession.”

verses.zh: 我只得死在这地，不能过约旦河；但你们必过去得那美地。
verses.en: So I must die here in this land; I will not cross the Jordan. But you are going over and will possess that[NOTE:1] good land.
notes: Heb “this.” The translation uses “that” to avoid confusion; earlier in the verse Moses refers to Transjordan as “this land.”

verses.zh: 你们要谨慎，免得忘记耶和华―你们　神与你们所立的约，为自己雕刻偶像，就是耶和华―你　神所禁止你做的偶像；
verses.en: Be on guard so that you do not forget the covenant of the Lord your God that he has made with you, and that you do not make an image of any kind, just as he[NOTE:1] has forbidden[NOTE:2] you.
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 4:3.
Heb “commanded.”

verses.zh: 因为耶和华―你的　神乃是烈火，是忌邪的　神。
verses.en: For the Lord your God is a consuming fire; he is a jealous God.[NOTE:1]
notes: The juxtaposition of the Hebrew terms אֵשׁ (ʾesh, “fire”) and קַנָּא (qannaʾ, “jealous”) is interesting in light of Deut 6:15 where the Lord is seen as a jealous God whose anger bursts into a destructive fire. For God to be “jealous” means that his holiness and uniqueness cannot tolerate pretended or imaginary rivals. It is not petty envy but response to an act of insubordination that must be severely judged (see H. Peels, NIDOTTE 3:937-40).

verses.zh: 「你们在那地住久了，生子生孙，就雕刻偶像，彷佛甚么形像，败坏自己，行耶和华―你　神眼中看为恶的事，惹他发怒。
verses.en: After you have produced children and grandchildren and have been in the land a long time,[NOTE:1] if you become corrupt and make an image of any kind[NOTE:2] and do other evil things before the Lord your God that enrage him,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “have grown old in the land,” i.e., been there for a long time.
Heb “a form of anything.” Cf. NAB, NASB, NRSV, TEV “an idol.”
The infinitive construct is understood here as indicating the result, not the intention, of their actions.

verses.zh: 我今日呼天唤地向你们作见证，你们必在过约旦河得为业的地上速速灭尽！你们不能在那地上长久，必尽行除灭。
verses.en: I invoke heaven and earth as witnesses against you[NOTE:1] today that you will surely and swiftly be removed[NOTE:2] from the very land you are about to cross the Jordan to possess. You will not last long there because you will surely be[NOTE:3] annihilated.
notes: I invoke heaven and earth as witnesses against you. This stock formula introduces what is known form-critically as a רִיב (riv) or controversy pattern. It is commonly used in the ancient Near Eastern world in legal contexts and in the OT as a forensic or judicial device to draw attention to Israel’s violation of the Lord’s covenant with them (see Deut 30:19; Isa 1:2; 3:13; Jer 2:9). Since court proceedings required the testimony of witnesses, the Lord here summons heaven and earth (that is, all creation) to testify to his faithfulness, Israel’s disobedience, and the threat of judgment.
Or “be destroyed”; KJV “utterly perish”; NLT “will quickly disappear”; CEV “you won’t have long to live.”
Or “be completely” (so NCV, TEV). It is not certain here if the infinitive absolute indicates the certainty of the following action (cf. NIV) or its degree.

verses.zh: 耶和华必使你们分散在万民中；在他所领你们到的万国里，你们剩下的人数稀少。
verses.en: Then the Lord will scatter you among the peoples and there will be very few of you[NOTE:1] among the nations where the Lord will drive you.
notes: Heb “you will be left men (i.e., few) of number.”

verses.zh: 在那里，你们必事奉人手所造的神，就是用木石造成、不能看、不能听、不能吃、不能闻的神。
verses.en: There you will worship gods made by human hands—wood and stone that can neither see, hear, eat, nor smell.

verses.zh: 但你们在那里必寻求耶和华―你的　神。你尽心尽性寻求他的时候，就必寻见。
verses.en: But if you seek the Lord your God from there, you will find him, if, indeed, you seek him with all your heart and soul.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “mind and being.” See Deut 6:5.

verses.zh: 日后你遭遇一切患难的时候，你必归回耶和华―你的　神，听从他的话。
verses.en: In your distress when all these things happen to you in future days, if you return to the Lord your God and obey him[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “hear his voice.” The expression is an idiom meaning “obey,” occurring in Deut 8:20; 9:23; 13:18; 21:18, 20; 26:14, 17; 27:10; 28:1-2, 15, 45, 62; 30:2, 8, 10, 20.

verses.zh: 耶和华―你　神原是有怜悯的　神；他总不撇下你，不灭绝你，也不忘记他起誓与你列祖所立的约。
verses.en: (for he[NOTE:1] is a merciful God), he will not let you down[NOTE:2] or destroy you, for he cannot[NOTE:3] forget the covenant with your ancestors that he confirmed by oath to them.
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 4:3.
Heb “he will not drop you,” i.e., “will not abandon you” (cf. NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).
Or “will not.” The translation understands the imperfect verbal form to have an added nuance of capability here.

verses.zh: 「你且考察在你以前的世代，自　神造人在世以来，从天这边到天那边，曾有何民听见　神在火中说话的声音，像你听见还能存活呢？这样的大事何曾有、何曾听见呢？
verses.en: Indeed, ask about the distant past, starting from the day God created humankind[NOTE:1] on the earth, and ask[NOTE:2] from one end of heaven to the other, whether there has ever been such a great thing as this, or even a rumor of it.
notes: The Hebrew term אָדָם (ʾadam) may refer either to Adam or, more likely, to “man” in the sense of the human race (“mankind,” “humankind”). The idea here seems more universal in scope than reference to Adam alone would suggest.

The verb is not present in the Hebrew text but has been supplied in the translation for clarification. The challenge has both temporal and geographical dimensions. The people are challenged to (1) inquire about the entire scope of past history and (2) conduct their investigation on a worldwide scale.

verses.zh: a
verses.en: Have a people ever heard the voice of God speaking from the middle of fire, as you yourselves have, and lived to tell about it?

verses.zh: 神何曾从别的国中将一国的人民领出来，用试验、神迹、奇事、争战、大能的手，和伸出来的膀臂，并大可畏的事，像耶和华―你们的　神在埃及，在你们眼前为你们所行的一切事呢？
verses.en: Or has God[NOTE:1] ever before tried to deliver[NOTE:2] a nation from the middle of another nation, accompanied by judgments,[NOTE:3] signs, wonders, war, strength, power,[NOTE:4] and other very terrifying things like the Lord your God did for you in Egypt before your very eyes?
notes: The translation assumes the reference is to Israel’s God in which case the point is this: God’s intervention in Israel’s experience is unique in the sense that he has never intervened in such power for any other people on earth. The focus is on the uniqueness of Israel’s experience. Some understand the divine name here in a generic sense, “a god,” or “any god.” In this case God’s incomparability is the focus (cf. v. 35, where this theme is expressed).
Heb “tried to go to take for himself.”
Heb “by testings.” The reference here is the judgments upon Pharaoh in the form of plagues. See Deut 7:19 (cf. v. 18) and 29:3 (cf. v. 2).
Heb “by strong hand and by outstretched arm.”

verses.zh: 这是显给你看，要使你知道，惟有耶和华―他是　神，除他以外，再无别神。
verses.en: You have been taught that the Lord alone is God—there is no other besides him.

verses.zh: 他从天上使你听见他的声音，为要教训你，又在地上使你看见他的烈火，并且听见他从火中所说的话。
verses.en: From heaven he spoke to you in order to teach you, and on earth he showed you his great fire from which you also heard his words.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and his words you heard from the midst of the fire.”

verses.zh: 因他爱你的列祖，所以拣选他们的后裔，用大能亲自领你出了埃及，
verses.en: Moreover, because he loved[NOTE:1] your ancestors, he chose their[NOTE:2] descendants who followed them and personally brought you out of Egypt with his great power
notes: The concept of love here is not primarily that of emotional affection but of commitment or devotion. This verse suggests that God chose Israel to be his special people because he loved the patriarchs (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob) and had promised to bless their descendants. See as well Deut 7:7-9.

The LXX, Smr, Syriac, Targum, and Vulgate read a third person masculine plural suffix for the MT’s third person masculine singular, “his descendants.” Cf. Deut 10:15. Quite likely the MT should be emended in this instance.

verses.zh: 要将比你强大的国民从你面前赶出，领你进去，将他们的地赐你为业，像今日一样。
verses.en: to dispossess nations greater and stronger than you and brought you here this day to give you their land as your property.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “(as) an inheritance,” that is, landed property that one can pass on to one’s descendants.

verses.zh: 所以，今日你要知道，也要记在心上，天上地下惟有耶和华他是　神，除他以外，再无别神。
verses.en: Today realize and carefully consider that the Lord is God in heaven above and on earth below—there is no other!

verses.zh: 我今日将他的律例诫命晓谕你，你要遵守，使你和你的子孙可以得福，并使你的日子在耶和华―你　神所赐的地上得以长久。」
verses.en: Keep his statutes and commandments that I am setting forth[NOTE:1] today so that it may go well with you and your descendants and that you may enjoy longevity in the land that the Lord your God is about to give you as a permanent possession.
notes: Heb “commanding” (so NRSV).

verses.zh: 「那时，摩西在约旦河东，向日出之地，分定三座城，
verses.en: Then Moses selected three cities in the Transjordan, toward the east.

verses.zh: 使那素无仇恨、无心杀了人的，可以逃到这三城之中的一座城，就得存活：
verses.en: Anyone who accidentally killed someone[NOTE:1] without hating him at the time of the accident[NOTE:2] could flee to one of those cities and be safe.
notes: Heb “the slayer who slew his neighbor without knowledge.”
Heb “yesterday and a third (day).” The point is that there was no animosity between the two parties at the time of the accident and therefore no motive for the killing.

verses.zh: 为流便人分定旷野平原的比悉；为迦得人分定基列的拉末；为玛拿西人分定巴珊的哥兰。」
verses.en: These cities are Bezer, in the wilderness plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Manassehites.

verses.zh: 摩西在以色列人面前所陈明的律法―
verses.en: This is the law that Moses set before the Israelites.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the sons of Israel” (likewise in the following verse).

verses.zh: 就是摩西在以色列人出埃及后所传给他们的法度、律例、典章；
verses.en: These are the stipulations, statutes, and ordinances that Moses spoke to the Israelites after he had brought them out of Egypt,

verses.zh: 在约旦河东伯・毗珥对面的谷中，在住希实本、亚摩利王西宏之地；这西宏是摩西和以色列人出埃及后所击杀的。
verses.en: in the Transjordan, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of King Sihon of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon. (It is he whom Moses and the Israelites attacked after they came out of Egypt.

verses.zh: 他们得了他的地，又得了巴珊王噩的地，就是两个亚摩利王，在约旦河东向日出之地。
verses.en: They possessed his land and that of King Og of Bashan—both of whom were Amorite kings in the Transjordan, to the east.

verses.zh: 从亚嫩谷边的亚罗珥，直到西云山，就是黑门山。
verses.en: Their territory extended[NOTE:1] from Aroer at the edge of the Arnon valley as far as Mount Siyon[NOTE:2]—that is, Hermon—
notes: The words “their territory extended” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. In the Hebrew text vv. 47-49 are all one sentence, but for the sake of English style and readability the translation divides the text into two sentences.
Mount Siyon (the Hebrew name is שִׂיאֹן [siʾon], not to be confused with Zion [צִיּוֹן, tsiyyon]) is another name for Mount Hermon, also called Sirion and Senir (cf. Deut 3:9).

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 4:1-4

1"Now, O Israel, listen to the statutes and the judgments which I am teaching
you to perform, so that you may live and go in and take possession of the land which the Lord, the God of your
fathers, is giving you. 2You shall not add to the word which I am commanding you, nor take away from it, that you may keep the
commandments of the Lord your God which I command you. 3Your eyes have seen what the
Lord has done in the case of Baal-peor, for all the men who followed Baal-peor, the Lord your God has destroyed
them from among you. 4But you who held fast to the Lord your God are alive today, every one of you."

4:1 "listen" This VERB (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE) is used often
in Deuteronomy (e.g. Deut. 1:16; 4:1; 5:1; 6:3,4; 9:1; 20:3; 27:10; 33:7). Its basic meaning is "to hear so as to do." It focuses on action,
not just hearing (cf. James 1:22-25). This chapter has several warnings, Deut. 4:l, 2, 6, 9, 13, 14, 15, 19, 23, and 26 (cf. Micah 1:2; 3:1; 6:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ "the statutes and the judgments" These include the collective revelations of God. It is all that God
has revealed about Himself and His covenant requirements. It is similar in meaning to the word Torah (lit. "teachings,"
i.e. Mosaic legislation).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION (using DEUTERONOMY and PSALMS)

▣ "which I am teaching you" Moses served as YHWH's agent of deliverance and revelation (i.e. prophet,
cf. Deut. 3:14; 4:1-17; 18:15-18; 34:10-12).

▣ "to perform" The INFINITIVE (BDB 793, KB 889, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)
encourages the people to hear YHWH's law and then obey it (cf. Deut. 16:12; 30:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "so that they may go in and take possession of the land" Notice the conditional nature of YHWH's
covenant (e.g. Deut. 5:33; 8:1; 16:20; 30:16,19). All of thee VERBS are Qal PERFECTS. The
last VERB in Deut. 4:1 (giving) is a Qal PARTICIPLE. God's gift depends on Israel's actions!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND

▣ "the God of your fathers" This refers to the Patriarchs (Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, cf. Deut. 1:11,21;
4:1,31,37; 6:3; 12:1; 26:7; 27:3). All of the covenants with the Patriarchs involved conditions (except Genesis 6-9 and 15:12-21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

4:2 "you shall not add to the word. . .nor take away from it" This does not refer to scribes updating the text of
the Law, but rather that you cannot add to the essence of the Law (cf. Deut. 12:32; Prov. 30:5-6; Eccl. 3:14; Jer. 26:2; this
is similar to Rev. 22:18-19). These bans on "adding to" or "subtracting from" are characteristic of Ancient Near Eastern
literature. However, there is a slight difference between the Ten Words as recorded in Exodus 20 and Deuteronomy 5. See
Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 782-784.

4:3 "Baal-peor" This (BDB 128) refers to the place where Israelites turned from following YHWH and went after the
fertility gods of Moab (cf. Num. 25:1-9). The LXX and Peshitta translate this as referring to the local Ba'al.

4:4 "you who held fast to the Lord" The Hebrew word "hold," "cleave"
(BDB 180) is translated as a VERB in NASB. It is the opposite of "follow after" in
Deut. 4:3 (i.e. Ba'al). The VERB form of this word is used:

- of Adam's love for Eve ‒ Gen. 2:24

- of holding fast to YHWH ‒ Deut. 10:20; 11:22; 13:4; Josh. 22:5; 23:8; 2 Kgs. 18:6; Ps. 101:3

- of Boaz telling Ruth to stay close to his female servants ‒ Ruth 2:8, 21, 23

- of Solomon's idolatry to his young wives' gods ‒ 1 Kgs. 11:2

- of holding fast to YHWH's covenant ‒ Ps. 119:31

It denotes an attitude of loyalty or commitment. It is used in parallel with "love" in Gen. 34:3;
1 Kgs. 11:2; Prov. 18:24 (see NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 911).

Even in the election of YHWH, humans had to respond appropriately. Even as God chose
Israel to be His priestly nation (cf. Exod. 19:5-6), each individual had to choose God. This is a balance between God's
sovereignty and human freewill. It is also the balance of corporality ("you" PLURAL) versus individual
("everyone of you") response.

These is no VERB in Deut. 4:4; the VERBAL idea is conveyed by two
ADJECTIVES (BDB 180, 311).

5"See, I have taught you statutes and judgments just as the Lord
my God commanded me, that you should do thus in the land where you are entering to possess it. 6So keep and do them, for that is your
wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples who will hear all these statutes and say, 'Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.'
7For what great nation is there that has a god so near to it as is the Lord our God whenever we call on Him?
8Or what great nation is there that has statutes and judgments as righteous as this whole law which I am setting before you today?"

This is a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 906, KB 1157). It was a literary way of
asserting that Moses had fulfilled his responsibility and now the people must respond appropriately.

▣ "possess it" See SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND

There are two VERBS in this phrase:

- "keep" (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT with waw), which means "keep," "watch," or "preserve." This
VERB is used often in the Pentateuch (Deuteronomy, cf. Deut. 2:4; 4:2,6,9,15,23,40; many other places)

- "do" (BDB 793, KB 889, Qal PERFECT with waw) means "do" or "make." The VERB is also
used often in the OT (e.g. Deut. 4:1,3,6,13,14,16,23,25).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

4:6 "wisdom" This term (BDB 315) is used in Prov. 1:2,7 and the ADJECTIVE in Deut. 1:6. This
wisdom is knowledge of God and His will. It is what humans seek because they are made

- in the image and likeness of God (cf. Gen. 1:26-27)

- for fellowship with Him (cf. Gen. 3:8; Deut. 4:7-8)

▣ "understanding" This term (BDB 108) is parallel to wisdom. Its goal is an informed, godly, happy
life (e.g. Deut. 32:28; Prov. 2:1-22; 3:13-18).

▣ "Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people" Did YHWH choose Israel because He
loved them more than any others? He loves all humans equally (cf. Ezek. 18:23,32; 33:11; John 3:16; 1 Tim. 2:4;
2 Pet. 3:9). God simply needed a place to begin. He chose Abraham and his seed to be a kingdom of priests to the
world (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:4-6; Acts 3:25; Gal. 3:8). Theirs was an election for purpose rather than election
because of special love.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

4:7 "what great nation is there that has a god so near to it" This refers to YHWH's personal presence (i.e. immanence)
with Israel in the form of the Shekinah cloud (wilderness wandering period) and later the ark of the covenant
(beyond Jordan and into the monarchial period).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE CLOUD

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

▣ "whenever we call on Him" This shows that the Israelites had confidence that the God who made the
world was the God who would respond to them when they prayed. He is both powerful and personal (e.g. Ps. 34:18;
145:18)! A God who hears their prayers, and acts on their behalf, just opposite from the Canaanite idols!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON THE NAME

4:8 "statutes and judgments. . .law" Israel is unique among all the nations because of YHWH's covenant
presence and revelation. YHWH's character is revealed in His acts and laws.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "righteous" This is imagery from a river reed. God' righteousness is the
standard or ruler by which we are measured. The law is based on the character of God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "this whole law" This phrase refers to the book of Deuteronomy.

the Lord said to me, 'Assemble the people to Me, that I may let them hear My words so they may learn to fear Me

and judgments, that you might perform them in the land where you are going over to possess it."

This phrase has two IMPERATIVES from the same root:

- "give heed" ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Niphal IMPERATIVE, cf. Deut. 4:15; Josh. 23:11; Jer. 17:21).

- "keep" ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERATIVE in the sense of "keep by doing" (cf. Deut. 7:12).

For "soul," see SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH.

Obedience is a life-and-death issue (cf. Deut. 30:15-20)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

▣ "so that you do not forget. . .they do not depart" See Deut. 8:11-20.

▣ "heart" In Hebrew psychology the emotions are centered in the bowels. The heart is the center of
the intellect (especially memory) and personality. God is saying, "Do not forget the law!"

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

SPECIAL TOPIC: INWARD PARTS

▣ "all the days of your life" A lifestyle commitment is required (cf. Deut. 4:10; 6:2; 12:1; 16:3). Biblical faith
is not only an initial decision but a lifelong commitment.

▣ "make them known to your sons and your grandsons" This is a recurrent theme in Deuteronomy
(cf. Deut. 4:10; 6:7, 20-25; 11:19; 31:13; 32:46; and note Exod. 10:2; 12:26; 13:8,14). If believers do not teach their
children about YHWH, they are failures as parents (biblically speaking)! Faith runs through families (cf. Deut. 5:10; 7:9)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

4:10 "Remember the day you stood before the Lord your God at Horeb" This
refers to a previous generation. This specifically refers to Exodus 19-20. Remembering and passing on
YHWH's great acts of deliverance (i.e. exodus) is a recurrent theme (cf. Deut. 5:15; 7:18; 8:2,18; 9:7,27; 11:2; 15:15; 16:3,12;
24:9,18,22; 25:17; 32:7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOREB

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOCATION OF MT. SINAI

▣ "so they may learn to fear Me" YHWH acted as He did on Mt. Horeb so that they would hold Him in
reverential awe (cf. Exod. 20:20; Prov. 1:7; 9:10; Eccl. 12:15; Isa. 11:2-3; Ps. 34:11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

4:11 "the mountain burned with fire" Fire is a symbol of YHWH's presence (cf. Exod. 19:18; Deut. 5:23; 9:15;
Heb. 12:18). It may symbolize purity.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

▣ "darkness, cloud and thick gloom" YHWH's physical presence can be understood in two ways:

- volcanic activity ‒ Exod. 19:18; Ps. 68:7-8; 77:18; 97:2-5; Jdg. 5:4-5; 2 Sam. 22:8; Isa. 29:6; Jer. 10:10

- storm ‒ Exod. 19:16,19; Ps. 68:8; 77:18; Jdg. 5:4; Isa. 29:6; Nahum 1:3

- a supernatural event (i.e. Shekinah)

Therefore, the deep darkness (cf. Deut. 5:22; 2 Sam. 22:10; 1 Kgs. 8:12; 2 Chr. 6:1) might be:

- ash clouds

- rain clouds

This covering was for Israel's protection (cf. Exod. 19:18). They thought that if humans looked
upon God they would die (cf. Gen. 16:13; 32:30; Exod. 3:6; 20:19; 33:20; Jdg. 6:22-23; 13:22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEEP DARKNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: CAN HUMANS SEE GOD AND LIVE?

4:12 "but you saw no form" YHWH has no physical form (cf. John 4:24). He allowed Moses to see His
"afterglow" in Exod. 33:23. YHWH desires no physical representation because of fallen mankind's tendency
toward idolatry (cf. Deut. 4:15-19). See full note online at Exod. 33:17-23.

4:13 "He declared to you His covenant" This VERB (BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil
IMPERFECT with waw), when used with YHWH as the subject, denotes new revelation
(e.g. 2 Sam. 7:11; Isa. 42:9; 45:19; Amos 4:13).

The IMPERFECT tense implies that the "ten words" are not all of YHWH's revelation. Much
of the books of Exodus and Deuteronomy are explanations of the implications of the Decalog.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "Ten commandments" Literally this means "ten words" (BDB 797 CONSTRUCT 182) and is known
in Greek as the Decalogue. They are very brief, a summary of God's revelation (cf. Exodus 20; Deuteronomy 5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TEN COMMANDMENTS

▣ "He wrote them" YHWH Himself wrote (anthropomorphic) the "ten words" (cf. Exod. 31:8; 32:15-16).
Reflecting on the imagery of this statement does not affect the divine source of the commands!

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

▣ "two tablets of stone" From recent archaeological discoveries and what we call the Suzerain Hittite
Treaties (of the 2nd millennium B.C.), we know that Deuteronomy follows their outline and form. I think
that the "two tablets" refers to two, exact copies of the Ten Commandments required by these treaty patterns (also a
documenting of the past act of the major power making the treaty, i.e. Deuteronomy 1-4). This establishes the historicity
of Deuteronomy. See introduction to the book, VII.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN) TREATIES

4:14 "you might perform them" It is not enough to know God's will for your life, but to do it (cf. Deut. 4:1,2,5,6;
Luke 6:46; James 2:14-20). Biblical faith is a lifetime of faithful worship, obedience, and service, not a one-time religious event

▣ "possess it" See SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND

15"So watch yourselves carefully, since you did not see any form on
the day the Lord spoke to you at Horeb from the midst of the fire, 16so that you do not act
corruptly and make a graven image for yourselves in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female, 17the likeness
of any animal that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the sky, 18the likeness of anything that creeps
on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the water below the earth. 19And beware not to lift up your eyes to heaven
and see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of heaven, and be drawn away and worship them and serve them, those which the
Lord your God has allotted to all the peoples under the whole heaven. 20But the Lord
has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, from Egypt, to be a people for His own possession, as today.

"So watch yourselves carefully"

The VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Niphal PERFECT with waw) is used
in Deut. 4:2,6,9(twice),15,23,40. Israel's actions were conditionally connected to YHWH's covenant. They were to
strenuously avoid idolatry (cf. Deut. 5:8-10).

▣ "you did not see any form" See SPECIAL TOPIC: CAN HUMANS SEE GOD AND LIVE?).

▣ "at Horeb" see SPECIAL TOPIC: LOCATION OF MT. SINAI

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOREB

4:16 "act corruptly and make a graven image" This sin is a reference to the golden calf made by Aaron (cf. Exodus 32),
which violated YHWH's incorporality. The Israelites were not to represent YHWH by anything physical (cf. Deut. 4:16-18,23,25; 5:8; Exod. 20:4).

▣ "the likeness of male or female" Mankind's tendency has been to make YHWH like a man or woman. If we put
God in a human form, we have put Him into a form which we can manage.

4:17 "likeness of any animal" This may refer to

- other nations' use of animals to represent their gods and goddesses

- characteristics of animals to describe God

4:18 "creeps on the ground" This possibly refers to the Egyptian Scarab beetle which was holy to them.

4:19 "the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of heaven" The ancients, as well as the moderns
(horoscope), felt that the stars represented forces or powers that control the lives of humans. The worship of astral
bodies seems to have started in Babylon (Genesis 1 may represent a reaction to this type of idolatry, as Exodus 20
represents a reaction to Egyptian idolatry). Israel is to vigorously reject this kind of idolatry!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOON WORSHIP

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

▣ "those which the Lord your God has allotted to all the peoples" The
VERB (BDB 323, KB 322, Qal PERFECT) means "to divide," but in the sense of
allotment or apportionment. This could imply that God encouraged astral worship, but I think instead it is another
way to show YHWH's sovereignty over all heavenly bodies and all the earth (cf. Deut. 29:26; 32:8 in LXX). Astral idolatry was
never YHWH's plan or will for any human.

4:20 "the iron furnace" A furnace takes unusable ore, heats it and makes it usable metal. This is an analogy
of what YHWH did to Israel in Egypt (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:51; Jer. 11:4 and the same imagery in Isa. 48:10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD TESTS HIS PEOPLE (OT)

▣ "to be a people for His own possession" This was a special title for YHWH's covenant people
(e.g. Exod. 19:5; Deut. 7:6; 14:2; 26:18; Titus 2:14; and 1 Pet. 2:9). They have a divine inheritance (YHWH and land)
because YHWH had chosen them even before creation (cf. Deut. 32:8-9; Ps. 33:6-12; Jer. 10:16; 51:19) to represent
Himself to the world.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

21"Now the Lord was angry with me on your
account, and swore that I would not cross the Jordan, and that I would not enter the good land which the Lord
your God is giving you as an inheritance. 22For I will die in this land, I shall not cross the Jordan, but you shall cross and take
possession of this good land. 23So watch yourselves, that you do not forget the covenant of the Lord
your God which He made with you, and make for yourselves a graven image in the form of anything against which the Lord
your God has commanded you. 24For the Lord your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God."

4:21 "the Lord was angry with me on your account" Moses was reminding the
people of YHWH's punishment to him because of his disobedience (cf. Deut. 1:37; 3:26; Num. 20:7-13). If they disobey, they
will be punished also!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

4:23 "So watch yourselves" The VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Niphal IMPERATIVE)
is repeated often in this chapter. There are covenant benefits, but also covenant consequences (cf. Deut. 4:25; chapters 27-30;
Leviticus 26).

▣ "that you do not forget the covenant" The VERB (BDB 1013, KB 1489,Qal
PERFECT) is also found several times in this chapter (cf. Deut. 4:9,23,31) and also in
Deut. 6:12; 8:11,14,19[twice]; 9:7; 24:19[twice]; 25:19; and 30:13; 31:21; 32:18. This is a major recurrent theme!

4:24 "jealous" YHWH is described in this verse in two ways:

- "a consuming fire" (BDB 77 and BDB 37, KB 46, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, cf. Exod. 24:17;
Deut. 4:24; 9:3; Heb. 12:29) which denotes"

- YHWH is the covenant-making God of Sinai

- He is the God of judgment if the covenant is violated

- "a jealous God" (BDB 888 and 42, cf. Exod. 20:5; 34:14; Deut. 5:9; 6:15; Josh. 24:19) which denotes His
personal, loving commitment to Israel, which is analogous to a marriage covenant (cf. Hosea 1-3). The
covenant broken results in rejection (e.g. Josh. 24:19; Nahum 1:2). The word has a wide semantic field:

- passion ‒ Prov. 6:34; Song of Songs 8:6

- anger ‒ Prov. 14:30; 27:4

- jealousy ‒ Gen. 26:14; Num. 5:11-22; Ezek. 31:9

- competition ‒ Eccl. 4:4

- devotion ‒ Num. 11:29

(list from NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 938)

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUS. . .ZEALOUS

25"When you become the father of children and children's children and have
remained long in the land, and act corruptly, and make an idol in the form of anything, and do that which is evil in the sight of the Lord
your God so as to provoke Him to anger, 26I call heaven and earth to witness against you today, that you will surely perish quickly
from the land where you are going over the Jordan to possess it. You shall not live long on it, but will be utterly destroyed. 27The
Lord will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations where the Lord
drives you. 28There you will serve gods, the work of man's hands, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell. 29But
from there you will seek the Lord your God, and you will find Him if you search for Him with all your heart and all your soul.
30When you are in distress and all these things have come upon you, in the latter days you will return to the Lord your

They were part of the "eye for eye" justice system of Israel. If someone accidently killed a covenant
partner then that family had the legal right to kill him (i.e. the blood avenger of Num. 35:12; Deut. 19:6,12; Josh. 20:3,5,9). If
the one who accidentally killed another fled to one of these special cities, there was a trial by the elders; if he was
found not to be a premeditated murderer, then he could live in the city safely (until the death of the High Priest). Then he
could return to his home safely (in a legal sense).

Notice "across Jordan" is here qualified so as to refer to the eastern bank.
